transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18 15:30 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (Ironcrest Head of ML), Oliver Grant (CTO), Priya Reddy (Security Lead), Ethan Lowe (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick renewal check-in, discuss EU on-prem pilot scope, review security requirements, agree next steps for amendment and benchmark.

[00:00:07] Samir: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh we'll keep this tight, is the time still good on your end?
[00:00:13] Maya: yep, all good. we've got about 45mins, great.
[00:00:20] Samir: awesome. quick agenda: renewal numbers, onprem pilot scope in eu, security checklist and then next steps. Laura will run the tech bits.
[00:00:30] Oliver: sounds good. high level we're aligned on wanting a one-year extension but need regional onprem parity for latency sensitive use cases.
[00:00:45] Laura: cool. can you remind me of the primary SLA you care about — p95 latency, throughput or cost per token?
[00:00:52] Maya: latency is king for the clinical inference path. p95 under 120ms ideally; throughput is secondary but we need consistent tail performance. cost matters but we can't trade latency for 3x cheaper ops.
[00:01:10] Priya: and from security we need KMS integration, audit logs retained for 2 years, SSO/SAML with SCIM and evidence for SOC2 + ISO 27001. also data residency: EU only for the onprem pilot.
[00:01:30] Laura: got it. those are all within the typical ask. Redwood's private package supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs, we can keep control plane off your VPC if you prefer full tenancy.
[00:01:45] Ethan: small nit - when you say "private package" are we talking vendor-hosted VPC or fully onprem? we have air-gapped requirements for certain workloads.
[00:01:55] Samir: good question. there are two paths: a VPC-hosted private deployment (we manage infra in your cloud region) or an onprem appliance. for Ironcrest we talked about a pilot that'd be onprem in eu-west, with our control plane in a customer-managed VPC.
[00:02:12] Oliver: yes -- pilot must run inside our datacenter for the first phase, then if all goes well we'll consider a managed VPC stage.
[00:02:22] [00:02:22] Laura: technically we can do the onprem artifact as a containerized bundle plus an ops-runbook; it needs GPU access (NVIDIA A10/A100 class), kube rn etes or a simple docker-compose for the pilot, and we include token-level tracing hooks so you can map cost back to services.
[00:02:40] Maya: ok, the team already has A100s; we'll confirm exact SKU. I'm mostly worried about the KV cache and checkpointing — if we lose a node what's the warmup cost?
[00:02:55] Laura: good point. our runtime supports persistent KV cache and warm-starts; for the onprem pilot we recommend a 2-replica setup for the model shards and a shared NFS or nvme-backed volume for KV persistence. transcribed in notes as "KV cash" earlier, sorry for that.
[00:03:15] Ethan: that helps. re: quantization — do you support 4-bit quant on the onprem runtime? we've got memory limits.
[00:03:23] Laura: yes, we have quantization profiles. for production we usually recommend 4-bit FP8-ish configs for throughput but we can run both quant and fp16 variants and fall back when accuracy regs flag an issue.
[00:03:36] [00:03:36] Maya: accuracy regressions are a no-go for the clinical model. we need rolling evals and a canary policy. can we set automatic rollback on quality drop?
[00:03:46] Laura: absolutely, Redwood's rollout supports canary, A/B and auto-fallback to last good variant based on eval triggers. you can plug in your eval suite and set thresholds.
[00:04:00] Samir: on the commercial side, for a retainer extension we can provide a tiered band: baseline reserved capacity + burst pool. baseline gives you guaranteed throughput; burst is best-effort with fallbacks.
[00:04:15] Oliver: what's the rough delta on price if we go fully onprem versus VPC private?
[00:04:21] Samir: onprem has higher one-time engineering/support fees (packaging, on-site enablement) but the monthly retainer can be lower because infra costs are yours. VPC private keeps less lift for you but slightly higher monthly. I'll send a numbered band so it's easier to compare.
[00:04:36] Priya: procurement will push back on long lead times. what timelines are we looking at for a 2-week pilot to go live?
[00:04:44] Laura: assuming you have the GPUs and network prep, we can target a 2-week technical pilot from kickoff: week 0 prep, week 1 deploy + smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks and handover. so about 14–21 days.
[00:05:00] Ethan: sounds reasonable. we need a runbook for firewall rules, allowed egress, and a list of ports.
[00:05:08] Laura: we'll provide a hardened runbook. we'll also include required kube rn etes configs, sample helm chart, and the kernel/driver versions we've validated.
[00:05:22] [00:05:22] Maya: one wrinkle — we have an internal cost committee that compares BigCloudAI's managed offering which noted a 20% lower quoted monthly. they don't take the latency delta into account though.
[00:05:34] Samir: understood. we'll come back with clear latency vs cost tradeoffs and a sample economics sheet that maps tokens -> $/month under your workload profile.
[00:05:46] Oliver: also, we're required to present evidence of encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and details about KMS key rotation cadence for the board.
[00:05:54] Priya: yes and we need clarity on who has access to audit logs and how RBAC maps to our AD groups.
[00:06:03] Laura: we support AD/SAML via SSO + SCIM, RBAC can be synced to your groups. Audit logs are stored to your S3-compatible bucket; retention configurable up to multi-year. KMS calls can be routed to your HSM.
[00:06:16] Ethan: can we do HSM on day one for the pilot or is that later?
[00:06:20] Laura: HSM integration is doable in pilot but usually it's phase 2 if you want vendor-managed HSM. if you're bringing your own HSM in the DC it's usually faster.
[00:06:32] [00:06:32] Maya: ok. small ask — can Laura run a short benchmark now-ish to show p95 numbers on a representative sample? we can schedule but some rough past numbers help the committee.
[00:06:44] Laura: i can share historical p95 numbers for similar models: ~85–110ms p95 on an A100 with sequence lengths like yours. but i want to be clear that the sample payload matters — please share a small trace set.
[00:06:58] Samir: noted as an action.
[00:07:05] Oliver: from contract terms: we want a 12-month extension with an option to increase baseline capacity at 90 days. is that feasible?
[00:07:14] Samir: yes, we can add a volume uptick clause at 90 days with pre-agreed pricing tiers.
[00:07:20] Priya: and what about liability and data breach responsibilities for the onprem appliance — how does that read?
[00:07:27] Samir: the onprem model typically assigns responsibility for data once inside your network; Redwood supports the software and warranty. procurement/legal will put the exact SLAs and indemnities in the amendment. we'll make sure security gets the standard exhibit.
[00:07:41] [00:07:41] Diego: quick ops note — for pilot telemetry we'll enable token-level cost traces but redact PHI; we should confirm the PII/PHI handling with Maya.
[00:07:50] Maya: yes we'll send our redaction rules.
[00:07:56] Laura: thank you. also we'll include a short script to mask sensitive spans before telemetry leaves the DC. it's in our onprem ops kit.
[00:08:07] [00:08:07] Oliver: procurement also asked about transition support — if pilot fails, what's reverse migration?
[00:08:14] Samir: we'll include a rollback plan; if pilot doesn't meet thresholds we can decommission and provide a data export tool. cost for decommissioning is usually covered in the pilot engineering budget.
[00:08:28] Maya: good. i'm going to quickly outline the pilot scope so we're aligned: 1) deploy one model shard cluster in our EU DC, 2) run 2-week smoke + benchmark using real traces, 3) evaluate p95 and quality via our evals, 4) report and decide go/no-go. does that reflect what you heard?
[00:08:47] Laura: yes that's accurate. add that we'll instrument canary rollouts and auto fallback during the pilot.
[00:08:54] Maya: yep.
[00:09:00] [00:09:00] Samir: ok timeline and owners — i'll send draft amendment + pricing by next wednesday, laura will share SOC2 packet and KMS notes by Monday, ironcrest to provide infra traces and GPU SKUs by Dec 30. pilot kickoff target Jan 10 pending signoff.
[00:09:18] Priya: who will be the exec sponsor from Redwood for escalation?
[00:09:23] Samir: Diego will be the CSM lead and i'm the commercial owner; i'll loop in our Director of Security if needed — name is Rowan Ellis, i'll copy them on the SOC2 package.
[00:09:36] [00:09:36] Ethan: small tech Q — does the runtime need specific kernel patches for A100? we've had driver mismatches before.
[00:09:44] Laura: we publish the validated driver matrix; for A100 generally driver >= 510.x and CUDA 11.4+. we'll put the exact versions in the runbook.
[00:09:55] Maya: perfect.
[00:10:00] [00:10:00] (brief silence as notes are transcribed)
[00:10:18] Oliver: procurement will also want to know about competitor posture — BigCloudAI offers lower price but less transparency. are there any big technical differences?
[00:10:27] Laura: most competitors do managed endpoints; Redwood emphasizes transparent perf meta, rollout tooling, and caching that reduces unit cost for steady-state workloads. we'll share a short comparison slide.
[00:10:40] Samir: i'll include a one-pager comparing latency/cost and the operational tradeoffs.
[00:10:48] [00:10:48] Maya: ok, last question from me — support SLAs during pilot?
[00:10:53] Diego: pilot includes 24/7 on-call for the deployment window with a named engineer and a 2-hour P1 response during the pilot. for prod we can negotiate an SLA.
[00:11:04] Maya: that works.
[00:11:08] [00:11:08] Priya: quick compliance Q — will we get a noise-free audit log for all admin ops? our auditors demand immutability.
[00:11:15] Laura: yes audit logs are append-only and we can set write-only permissions to your retention bucket; if you need a tamper-evident chain we can sign logs with your KMS keys.
[00:11:26] Ethan: really appreciate that detail.
[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Samir: ok we're at about 30 minutes; wanted to check if there are any other blockers on your side.
[00:11:37] Maya: none from me. procurement will review once we have the amendment.
[00:11:41] Oliver: legal will want a short window to review the amendment, probably 5 business days.
[00:11:47] Samir: understood. we'll aim to deliver docs early next week to give you time.
[00:11:54] [00:11:54] Diego: to recap: deliverables — amendment + pricing (Samir), SOC2/ISO + KMS notes (Laura), runbook + driver matrix (Laura), sample telemetry and traces (Ironcrest), pilot kickoff calendar (Diego).
[00:12:12] Maya: yes that's clear.
[00:12:16] Samir: any final quick clarifications?
[00:12:20] Priya: i just want the SOC2 evidence to show our auditors. if you can include the control mapping table that's very helpful.
[00:12:27] Laura: will do.
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Samir: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the timeline and attach the docs.
[00:12:36] Oliver: thanks all.
[00:12:40] Maya: thanks.

Action recap (auto): Samir to send amendment and pricing, Laura to share security docs and runbook, Ironcrest to provide GPU SKUs and traces, Diego to schedule pilot kickoff.

End of transcript.
